source.author: ov
source.text: Quam satis ad superas postquam Rhodopeius auras deflevit vates, ne non temptaret et umbras, ad Styga Taenaria est ausus descendere porta; perque leves populos simulacraque functa sepulcro Persephonen adiit inamoenaque regna tenentem umbrarum dominum.
source.text_original: Quam satis ad superas postquam Rhodopeius auras / deflevit vates, ne non temptaret et umbras, / ad Styga Taenaria est ausus descendere porta; / perque leves populos simulacraque functa sepulcro / Persephonen adiit inamoenaque regna tenentem / umbrarum dominum.
source.text_english: After the Rhodopeian bard had wept enough to the upper air, lest he should not also try the shades, he dared to descend to Styx by the Taenarian gate; and through the light peoples and the images that had fulfilled the tomb, he approached Persephone and the lord of the shades, who holds the unlovely realms.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: populumne levem veterique tyranno infensum atque olim miserantes Aesona patres advocet?
reuse.text_original: populumne levem veterique tyranno / infensum atque olim miserantes Aesona patres / advocet?
reuse.text_english: Should he summon a fickle people, hostile to the old tyrant, and the fathers of Aeson, who long ago had pity?
